summary: Customer private deploy: BPF-based flowlog agent enabling promiscuous mode -> RPS/RFS CPU steering change causing gRPC packet resequencing and KV-cache divergence
description: Issue summary: After a customer-installed BPF-based flowlog/monitoring agent was deployed in their private VPC, several serving nodes in the customer's private deploy began exhibiting transient gRPC stream resequencing. Symptoms included repeated token-cache misses, partial model shard re-fetches, and application-layer 5xxs on long-lived streaming requests. Impact: Customer reports elevated request latencies and a ~12% increase in failed streaming sessions for production traffic to the Llama2-13B-v2 model in us-east-1. This is customer-impacting for their production workload.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy the customer's BPF flowlog agent with default config (includes packet capture + promiscuous flag enabled) on hosts in the private VPC.
2) Start sustained production workload hitting streaming chat endpoints using pinned model 'llama2-13b-v2'.
3) Observe gRPC stream retransmits and application-layer retries within 2-10 minutes.
4) Collect tcpdump and ethtool/RPS counters on the affected ENI node.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: packet duplication or reordering at kernel/driver level due to promiscuous-mode BPF hooks interacting with NIC Gro/Gso and RPS/RFS steering.
- Customer confirmed they deployed a third-party flowlog agent (v2.1.4) which uses kernel BPF tc/ingress hooks and enables promiscuous mode to capture mirrored traffic.
- Observed elevated rx_packets twice as high as expected on affected ENI.
- Kernel RPS/RFS CPU masks show non-uniform steering after agent install; many packets steered to a CPU not running serving process leading to out-of-order handoff between RX and processing cores.
- gRPC traces show out-of-order sequence numbers and occasional retransmits; KV cache invalidations correlate with retransmit windows.
- No changes in our serving runtime or model artifacts detected in same window.
- Reproduced locally in customer's staging by toggling agent's promiscuous option: with promiscuous off, symptoms disappear in 3m; with on, resequencing and 5xxs return.
logs:
- /var/log/agent/flowlog.log: 'interface eth0: set promiscuous mode ON' at 2026-03-09T22:14:05Z
- kernel ring buffer snippet: 'eth0: GRO: packet reordering detected: rps rcpu mismatch' repeated
- tcpdump (sample): see packet timestamps showing small out-of-order delivery across same TCP connection (captured pcap attached by customer: ds_flowlog_bpf_0310.pcap)
- serving runtime logs: 'kvcache: shard-read mismatch; initiating re-fetch' and 'grpc: stream reset due to duplicate-seq'
- agent metrics: flowlog_agent.capture.packets_total spike from 1.2M -> 2.6M per minute after deploy

root_cause: Third-party BPF-based flowlog agent enabled promiscuous mode which changed packet processing path and interacted with NIC/GRO and kernel RPS/RFS CPU steering. This caused micro reordering of packets handed to the serving process, leading to gRPC-level resequencing/retransmits and subsequent KV-cache coherence failures in the serving runtime.
workaround: Customer-side immediate mitigations applied: 1) Set flowlog agent 'promiscuous_mode' = false (agent config change). 2) Set sysctl net.core.rps_sock_flow_entries=32768 and pin rps_cpu masks for ENI to CPUs hosting serving processes. 3) Disable GRO for eth interface: 'ethtool -K eth0 gro off' if acceptable for their throughput. These reduced errors to baseline in staging and prod when applied carefully.
resolution: In progress: agreed mitigation path with customer. Customer has rolled agent config change (promiscuous_mode=false) and applied RPS pinning on 60% of affected nodes; error rate fell to <2% above baseline. Engineering action items: (a) add detection in agent healthcheck to flag promiscuous mode BPF installs; (b) create a runbook for customers describing recommended kernel tunables when using BPF capture; (c) add serving-runtime guard to tolerate brief resequencing windows without cache invalidation. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/1786 (adds warning and config validation).
